r.정치 구도: The military took power in back-to-back coups in 2020 and 2021. The junta repeatedly postponed its promise to hand power to civilians, and in 2025 it dissolved all political parties and passed a law giving the junta leader a five-year term without an election. Since Tuareg rebels and Islamist armed groups rose up in the north in 2012, large parts of the north and center have slipped out of government control. From autumn 2025 an al-Qaeda-linked group blocked fuel convoys headed for the capital, leaving Bamako short of fuel, and in April 2026 it attacked Bamako and the nearby garrison town of Kati. The junta has rallied support by expelling foreign troops and putting sovereignty first, while opposition politicians and journalists have been arrested or forced into exile.

t.why: Mali lies at the heart of the Sahel, the southern edge of the Sahara, and is the center of the Islamist insurgency that has spread across the region. When armed groups pushed south in 2013, France, the former colonial power, sent troops, but after falling out with the junta it withdrew in 2022. UN peacekeepers left in 2023 at the junta's demand, and the gap was filled by Russia's Wagner mercenaries and, from 2025, by the Africa Corps under Russia's defense ministry. Together with Niger and Burkina Faso it formed the Alliance of Sahel States, and their exit from the Economic Community of West African States in 2025 reshaped the region. As one of Africa's leading gold producers, its tug-of-war with foreign companies over mining revenue is also a regular international story.
t.rel: It formed the Alliance of Sahel States with Niger and Burkina Faso and left ECOWAS. Relations with Algeria have soured badly over armed groups in the north and the downing of a drone. A landlocked country, it brings in goods through the ports of Senegal and Ivory Coast.
t.know: The Great Mosque of Djenne is the world's largest mud-brick building, and residents re-plaster it together every year.
etext: One of Africa's leading gold producers, Mali relies on gold for most of its exports. A 2023 mining code raised taxes and the state's stakes, pitting the government against foreign miners such as Canada's Barrick, and gold was even seized. The dispute ended in late 2025 when Barrick accepted the new code and paid a settlement.
Most people live from farming and herding. Water from the Niger River irrigates rice, and its cotton output ranks among the largest in Africa.
Lithium production began at the Goulamina mine in the south in 2024, giving Mali a new export after gold. A Chinese company developed the mine.

With no coastline, goods come in through ports in Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire. When armed groups block roads, fuel and supplies are cut off, and power shortages often shut factories and shops. Strained ties with neighbors and the West have also reduced aid and investment.
